why: Source: read the price to the restaurant, take 10% of it, divide by the preparation cost, pick the nearest option (4 steps); question: read the price to Formetal, take 10%, divide by the stamping cost, pick the nearest option (4 steps), so the path is identical.

Source: see that driver growth is total times share, then check four statements (greatest Productivity, least Productivity, least Hours, a 24% figure that needs no calculation), about 5 steps; question: the same recognition and the same four kinds of check on the same kind of labelled stacked bar (5 steps).

Source: triple the existing count, take the new-customer share at rating 4, take the existing share at rating 4, subtract (4 steps); question: triple the 22,000, take 20% of it, take 25% of 22,000, subtract (4 steps), with the same chart and the same trap of picking the right panel.

Source: packs to units, a discount threshold check, a mL-to-L price conversion and value for each size, then the average (about 5 steps); question: cases to bottles, the same threshold check, the same conversion and value for each size, then the average (5 steps).

Source: profit for each period from revenue minus costs, divide each by items sold, then the percentage change and a pick (about 5 steps); question: the same subtractions, per-bouquet divisions and percentage change (5 steps), with the same printed-margin distractor.

Source: read the price to the restaurant, take 10%, divide by the preparation cost, pick the nearest option (4 steps); question: read the price to Rindery, take 10%, divide by the cutting and wrapping cost, pick the nearest option (4 steps), so the path is identical.

Source: profit for each period from revenue minus costs, divide by items, then the percentage change (about 5 steps); question: the same subtractions, per-appointment divisions and percentage change (5 steps); only the direction of the change is reversed.

Source: four statement checks (past growth against the rest, three times the growth pace, under 10% share four years ago, a 20-year extrapolation compared), each with its own calculation (about 4 to 5 steps); question: the same four kinds of statement on the same kind of table (4 to 5 steps), with the true one now the past-growth comparison instead of the extrapolation.

Source: value of 1% of the larger cost base, value of 1% of the smaller base (the sub-cost option dominated), net gain from 1% more income after the linked cost rises, then compare (4 steps); question: the same three valuations and comparison (4 steps), with the answer moving to the income option but with the same linked-cost trap.

Source: pick the right pie, add the shares for ratings 1 to 3, multiply by the 15% respondent rate (3 steps); question: pick the right pie among four, add three shares, multiply by 12% (3 steps), so the path is identical.
